paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa's birth at Gokula, the festival, and his infancy and boyhood — bathing, cradling, the moon called to play, his pranks and the cowherds' complaints — sung in the voice of Yaśodā and the cowherd women.
speaker: Periyāḻvār as Yaśodā
notes: Centum-level summary; the first Tamil piḷḷaittamiḻ (child-poem) on the Lord.

paraphrase: Lord reclining on the serpent at Araṅgam: those who seek refuge with the strong find them no help in weakness; so I tell you now, for that hour when, at death, I shall be unable to call you — protect me then.
speaker: Periyāḻvār
notes: 'appoḻutaikku ippoḻutē colli vaittēṉ'. Śrīvaiṣṇavas read it with the Varāha carama-śloka ('I remember my devotee'). Content recalled with confidence; exact verse number to verify.

paraphrase: Lord of cool Tiruvēṅkaṭam, you stamped me and all that is mine with the mark of your discus and took me as your own; now I live by your grace alone.
speaker: Periyāḻvār
notes: Read by Śrīvaiṣṇavas as an early witness to the discus-branding (tāpa) of the five sacraments. Content moderate; verse number low.
